items.prompt: Simplify \(\frac{a^{3}\times a^{4}}{a^{2}}\), assuming \(a\ne 0\). Give the result as a single power of \(a\).

mark_scheme.text: Add exponents when multiplying equal bases.

items.prompt: Use prime factorisation to find both the highest common factor and the lowest common multiple of \(84\) and \(126\). Show enough working to justify both answers.

mark_scheme.text: Produce a correct prime factorisation or equivalent common-divisor method.

items.prompt: A right circular cylinder has radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and height \(4\text{ cm}\). Calculate its exact volume in terms of \(\pi\), with units.
Solve \(\frac{x+1}{2}=4\) without using a calculator. Show how you remove the denominator.
Simplify \(\frac{x^2-4}{x^2-2x}\) by factorisation. State all excluded values of \(x\) in the original expression.
Two sides of a triangle are \(8\text{ cm}\) and \(10\text{ cm}\). The angle between them is \(30^\circ\). Find its exact area using trigonometry, including units.
Let \(f(x)=2x+3\) and \(g(x)=x^2+1\). Simplify both \(f(g(x))\) and \(g(f(x))\), showing substitutions.

mark_scheme.text: Substitute f(x) into g and expand the square.

items.prompt: A bag contains 4 red counters and 3 blue counters. Two counters are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are red, giving a simplified exact fraction. Explain why the second probability changes.
Solve simultaneously \[\begin{aligned}y&=x+1\\x^2+y^2&=13\end{aligned}\] Give both ordered pairs. Verify one pair in the original circle equation.

mark_scheme.text: Verify at least one by substituting to obtain \(13\).

items.prompt: Rationalise the denominator of \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}-1}\). Give your answer in exact surd form and show why the denominator becomes rational.

mark_scheme.text: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate \(\sqrt{5}+1\).
Use the difference of squares to obtain denominator \(5-1=4\).

items.prompt: The first four terms of a sequence are \(6\), \(11\), \(18\), \(27\). Find an expression for its \(n\)th term and explain how the second differences support your method.

mark_scheme.text: Deduce that the coefficient of n² is half the second difference.
Substitute initial terms to determine the linear and constant coefficients.

items.prompt: Two similar solid shapes have corresponding lengths in the ratio \(2:3\) (smaller : larger). The smaller solid has volume \(16\text{ cm}^3\). Calculate the volume of the larger solid and explain why the length ratio must be cubed.

mark_scheme.text: Cube the linear scale factor for volumes.
